Do not cover whether the 31-facet model transfers cleanly at the conceptual level — that belongs to fd-personality-sim-facet-transfer

decision_lens: A Rust library extraction is not an organisational move — it is a contract change. Every pub item becomes a semver promise. Path dependencies hide API instability that crates.io publication will expose. The moment shadow-work's Agent holds a SoulId instead of an AgentPersonality struct, every downstream match on AgentPersonality variants breaks. The risk is not in the design; it is in the gap between 'works in the workspace' and 'works when locked by cargo'.
focus: Cargo workspace topology, API surface design for personality-engine extraction, workspace-vs-published-crate tradeoffs, extraction failure modes specific to Rust
name: fd-rust-cargo-workspace-extraction
persona: Apply the perspective of a Rust ecosystem architect who has managed multi-crate workspace extractions, published crates to crates.io with downstream consumers, and debugged the semver-surface problems that arise when a working-code library is promoted to a published dependency.
review_areas: The doc proposes three extraction shapes (A: published crate, B: workspace path dependency, C: reverse migration) and recommends B+C now with A later. But the brainstorm does not address the workspace topology question it defers: does 'one workspace' mean a monorepo (shadow-work and palettice merged into one git repo), a git submodule arrangement, a separate meta-repo, or two repos with a Cargo.lock-pins-path approach? Each has distinct CI, ownership, and fork-safety implications. The deferred extraction-shape Open Question leaves the migration plan underspecified at the git/workspace layer, which is where Rust extraction failures actually bite.

Shadow-work's AgentPersonality struct is described as the reference implementation that Palettice Phase 2 absorbs. But Rust does not have a clean 'absorb' primitive: either shadow-work re-exports Palettice types (requiring shadow-work to depend on Palettice), or Palettice grows types that shadow-work switches to (requiring shadow-work to be edited everywhere AgentPersonality is destructured or pattern-matched). The doc does not distinguish these — calling both paths 'migration' — but their impact on shadow-work's existing test suite and call sites differs radically. The pattern-match surface area for a 31-field struct that has survived real gameplay is substantial.

The doc lists six Palettice expansion items in dependency order but does not specify which require a breaking Palettice API change. FacetCatalogueId registration (item 1) and FacetEvolutionPolicy (item 2) both require additions to the Soul API surface. If Palettice is a path dependency (option B), breaking changes are refactored across the workspace in one commit. If it becomes a published crate mid-migration (option A transition), these become major version bumps that must be coordinated with shadow-work's Cargo.lock. The sequencing risk is not acknowledged.

The LlmCurated cost-hint derivation for ship names requires an actual LLM call path registered in the derivation system. The doc notes the invalidation strategy: re-roll when a significant scar lands, not every tick. But in Rust, a DerivationFn is typically a pure Fn — integrating async LLM calls into a synchronous derivation registry requires either a blocking executor call (unsound in async contexts) or a redesign of the DerivationFn signature to be async-capable. This is an API-surface question the doc treats as a configuration question, and the two are not the same.

The doc does not specify where Palettice's FacetCatalogue will live in the crate graph. If FacetCatalogue is in the core palettice crate, shadow-work's 31 facets become a compile-time dependency of palettice, which inverts the intended layering (palettice should not know about shadow-work's domain model). If they are in a separate palettice-shadow-catalogue crate, that crate needs to be created, versioned, and owned. The layering question is not resolved and it affects every item in the expansion roadmap.

severity_examples.condition: If the git/workspace topology question is not answered before migration begins, shadow-work's CI will break the first time a Palettice API changes, because there is no agreed mechanism for keeping the two repos in sync. Option B (workspace path dependency) requires a topology decision before it can be implemented; the brainstorm defers topology but names B as the recommendation, which is inconsistent.
severity_examples.scenario: Workspace topology left unresolved before migration starts

severity_examples.condition: Shadow-work has 31 personality facets working in production with tests. Any Rust migration that replaces AgentPersonality with a Soul-backed model requires finding every destructure, match, and field access on the old struct. The brainstorm treats this as assumed-tractable without acknowledging the risk. If shadow-work's codebase has 50+ pattern-match sites, the migration is not 'swap personality module' — it is a full rewrite of the personality call graph.
severity_examples.scenario: AgentPersonality pattern-match sites not enumerated before migration

severity_examples.condition: A synchronous DerivationFn that calls an LLM is architecturally unsound in an async game sim. If this is not resolved at the API design stage, the ship-name derivation will require a workaround (tokio::task::block_in_place, a pre-computed cache, or an async derivation registry redesign) that was not planned for.
severity_examples.scenario: LlmCurated derivation treated as configuration rather than API design

success_hints: Check whether the three extraction shape options map cleanly to actual Cargo features (workspace members, path deps, [patch] overrides) and flag any that assume git infrastructure not yet in place
Look for places where the doc says 'absorbs' or 'grows' Palettice to cover shadow-work's types — these require concrete Rust refactor steps the brainstorm has not named

Verify that each Palettice expansion item is characterised as either additive (no breaking change) or breaking, since that determines whether option B and A can transition without a major version bump
Flag any derivation described as involving external I/O (LLM, database lookup) that is being treated as a pure synchronous computation
task_context: The document is a brainstorm-stage design record proposing a migration of shadow-work's personality system into Palettice, alongside an expansion roadmap. This review focuses on whether the Rust-specific extraction mechanics are sound: workspace topology, API surface tradeoffs, pattern-match migration risk, and async integration concerns for derived values.
